title: 'If you're building a company with a mission geared towards human flourishing, this is the book to read.'
summary: NAOTAKE MURAYAMA — Stanford GSB alum, entrepreneur — publishes a 2,525-character Goodreads review connecting Incorruptible to Built to Last as the book that revitalized his aspiration to build something remarkable. Frames the book as the integrated approach that goes beyond visionary founders, beyond culture, beyond creative governance structures — all of them together, inseparable from the non-shareholder value the company creates.
blockquote:
If you're building a company with a mission geared towards human flourishing, this is the book to read.

Eric Ries' follow-up to "The Lean Startup" is no sequel; it goes above and beyond making startups successful, and provides us with inspiring models of companies that defy the constant and seemingly inevitable "Financial Gravity" - the pull of shareholder value and conventional fiduciary duty that "corrupt" their mission to make the world a better place.
